newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County supervisors to back Calif. tax measure.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County supervisors to back Calif. tax measure.

text.p: A tax initiative on California's November ballot would provide Los Angeles County with more over $100 million for local services, supporters of the measure said on Tuesday.
Proposition 217 would raise the revenues by keeping the top income tax brackets -- which expire this year -- in place for the wealthiest 1.0 percent of California taxpayers.

If the initiative is passed on November 5 more than $125 million would go to Los Angeles County in the first year for local services such as police and fire safety, libraries and child protection, supporters of the proposition said.
Cities in the county will receive more than $39 million.

Los Angeles County Supervisors Zev Yaroslavsky, Yvonne Brathwaite Burke and Gloria Molina plan to kick off the campaign to pass the initiative later on Tuesday at a press conference at the county Hall of Administration.
Proposition 217 supporters said they have planned a grassroots information campaign.
Proponents of the measure said it would provide schools and communities statewide with $860 million in the first year and $700 million in each following year.
